::: section-question
Can a computer learn to spot a fracture?
:::

::: section-meta
About 25 min · notebook cells 14–22 · 1 exercise
:::

::: {.callout-tip .key-points title="In short"}
- Start from a model trained on everyday photos, then fine-tune it on our X-rays.
- `device=0` trains on one GPU; the GPU dashboard shows it working.
- Compare accuracy with a baseline. For imbalanced data, look at recall.
:::

## The model

We'll use **YOLOv8n-cls**, a small image classifier. Training one from scratch needs far more than 4,000 images, so we use **transfer learning**: start from a model that has seen over a million everyday photos, then fine-tune it on X-rays.

::: {.callout-note .deeper collapse="true" title="Going deeper: why does transfer learning work on X-rays?"}
Early layers learn general features such as edges and textures. Fine-tuning mostly adjusts the later layers, so far fewer examples are needed.
:::

## Training settings

```{.python filename="hpc-for-ai.ipynb"}
EPOCHS   = 50
IMG_SIZE = 512
BATCH    = 64
WORKERS  = 8
```

| Setting | What it means |
|---|---|
| `EPOCHS` | Times the model sees every training image |
| `IMG_SIZE` | Width and height of the square each image becomes |
